newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: ABC SHAKE-UP
The man who has recommended a shake-up for the ABC, Bob Mansfield, has urged more discussion within the organisation on the direction it should take.
Mr Mansfield's report has called for long-term certainty in Government funding for the ABC.

He's also recommended strengthening the ABC'S core activities, and making it more accountable, but stopped short of limiting the national broadcaster's role or introducing advertising and sponsorship.
Mr Mansfield says there's not been near enough discussion between management and the Board on what form the ABC should take in the next three to five years.
He says the Government needs to take into account the recommendations of the review, rather than just announcing a funding cut.
CRICKET
The Australian eleven for the fourth cricket test against the West Indies, starting tomorrow, will be finalised in the morning.
Selectors must decide whether to play six batsmen or use Michael Bevan as the seventh batsman and as a second spin bowler with Shane Warne.
Australian captain Mark Taylor says he believes Bevan is certain to be chosen
Meanwhile, Adelaide Oval is in perfect condition for tomorrow's start of the test.
Rain earlier in the week and warm days since have put the wicket and outfield in peak condition.
Adelaide Oval curator Les Burdett says the wicket will be flat, with variable bounce and should turn in later in the match.
PERTH MARRIAGE ON AFTER ALL
A young Perth couple is celebrating a court decision that they may go ahead with their marriage tomorrow.
Seventeen year-old Amie Willis, who's pregnant, needed the court's permission to marry her fiancee Adam Cooper because she's not yet 18, the legal age for marriage under Australian law.
The couple wanted to make sure their baby, due in June, was born in wedlock.
A Magistrate's decision that they couldn't marry was quashed by a Supreme Court judge, and the marriage has been approved after a brief private hearing in the Perth magistrates court.
Mr Cooper says the decision is just great, and he and Miss Willis are just happy it's all over.
He's thanked all their supporters.
LOMU NOT HANGING UP BOOTS JUST YET
Giant All-Black winner Jonah Lomu is philosophical about today's news that he's been ruled out of rugby union for at least six months with chronic kidney disease.
The problem was first diagnosed two years ago as a minor problem but has deteriorated over the last three months and doctors have given the All-black star a 50 per cent chance of recovering.
Lomu says he's had a few knocks in his career, and while this is a big one, it's a chance he has to take.
He doubts his playing days are over, a view shared by New Zealand coach John Hart who says Lomu could still make the England and Wales tour at the end of the year.
SOUVENIR HUNTERS A CONCERN AT BRYANT OPEN HOUSE
In Hobart the house of Port Arthur gunman Martin Bryant has attracted a steady stream of people this morning.
Fifteen minutes after opening for inspection, more than 60 people had filed through Bryant's former house in New Town.
Two security guards are patrolling the house to deter souvenir hunters.
